findings.title: CAUTION note overstates when the rolling-updates feature flag is required
findings.body: The newly added CAUTION block states unconditionally: 'While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This is placed directly under the 'Managing Keycloak Operator Updates' heading, before any explanation of the default behavior. However, the immediately following NOTE says that when `update.strategy` is left unset, the Operator defaults to mimicking the pre-existing (26.1 and older) behavior with no mention of needing the feature flag. This is corroborated by operator/src/test/java/.../UpgradeTest.java, where `createInitialDeployment` only enables the `rolling-updates` feature when an explicit `UpdateStrategy` (e.g. RECREATE) is configured, and returns early (without enabling the feature) when `updateStrategy == null`. So the feature flag is only required when explicitly setting `update.strategy`, not for using the Operator's update mechanism in general. As written, the CAUTION note will mislead readers into thinking they must always enable `rolling-updates` or the Operator will fail, even when relying on default behavior.

findings.title: Feature-disabled gating is only tested for the metadata subcommand, and exit code is never asserted
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only launches `UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME` without the feature flag and checks the error message. The identical feature-gating logic was also added to `UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run()` (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), but there is no test exercising the `check` subcommand with the feature disabled. Additionally, the test never asserts the actual exit code (`CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED` = 4), even though the documentation (docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc) explicitly documents exit code 4 as the contract for 'feature disabled', and this exit code is meant to be relied upon by automation. Without an assertion on the exit code and without coverage of the `check` subcommand, a regression in either path (e.g., wrong exit code, or the check subcommand silently allowing use when the feature is disabled) would not be caught by tests.

findings.title: Silent reassignment of RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 changes the exit-code contract for existing users
findings.body: This change moves `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and reuses 4 for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` code. Prior to this PR, any scripts/automation built against the previously-released preview `update-compatibility check` command that interpreted exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will now observe exit code 4 meaning 'feature disabled' and exit code 3 meaning 'recreate required' — a behavior change with no migration note, deprecation warning, or changelog entry in the diff. Even though the tool is labeled preview, this is a backward-incompatible change to a documented, script-facing contract (the exit codes are explicitly called out in docs/guides/server/update-compatibility.adoc as being safe to depend on), and should be called out explicitly (e.g., in release notes) so existing preview adopters are not silently broken.
